_readme: F1 acceptance capture — structure.lock scope narrowed whole-run -> per-batch
(src/indexer/index.ts). Compares directly against eval/baseline-locks.json,
which was captured BEFORE this fix and is the number this file must beat.
MAST_SPEC.md:822-826 asserts 'lock holding is per-file-parse (10-50ms), not
per-tool-call' — this file records how close F1 actually gets to that claim,
including where it still falls short (see summary.residual_limitation).
Source of the raw events: <stateDir>/lock-metrics.jsonl (src/store/lockMetrics.ts),
same instrumentation baseline-locks.json used. `raw_events` below is a small
representative sample (first/last of run-1's 340 events, all of run-2/run-3's
events) — the full 403-line file is preserved at
/Users/spikedpunchvictim/temp/mast-bench/f1-state/lock-metrics.jsonl for anyone
who wants the complete run.
To regenerate (same recipe as baseline-locks.json, run against the F1-fixed build):
1. pnpm -F mast build
2. Fresh state dir: mkdir <state> && mast init <corpus> --state-dir <state> --no-index
3. Whole-run capture: mast index <corpus> --state-dir <state> --phase1-only
(writes many 'index-run' acquired/released pairs to <state>/lock-metrics.jsonl
instead of one — that IS the fix, see summary.structure_acquisitions_per_run)
4. Full-reindex JIT contention: touch a corpus file, start a second
`mast index <corpus> --state-dir <state> --phase1-only` (no --incremental) in
the background, then probe staleness for that file (see f1-jit-probe.mjs in
/Users/spikedpunchvictim/temp/mast-bench) while it runs.
5. Realistic incremental JIT success: touch a handful of files, start
`mast index <corpus> --state-dir <state> --incremental --phase1-only` in the
background, probe staleness for one of the touched files while it runs.
6. Copy the relevant lines of <state>/lock-metrics.jsonl into `raw_events` and
recompute `summary`.

corpus.description: NestJS framework source, same disposable benchmark copy baseline-locks.json used

runs.label: run-1: cold full index (mast init --no-index, then mast index --phase1-only), F1-fixed build
runs.note: Total wall time is essentially unchanged (~8% faster, within run-to-run noise) — per-batch lock acquire/release churn did not materially slow the run, confirming the fix trades lock GRANULARITY, not throughput.

runs.label: run-2: second full (non-incremental) index against the already-populated corpus, to create a long contention window for a full-reindex JIT probe. Killed (SIGTERM) once probe results were captured — not needed to run to completion, same precedent as baseline-locks.json's run-2.
runs.note: Immediately preceded by appending a comment line to packages/core/injector/container.ts so its mtime/content diverged from the indexed record. IMPORTANT, UNEXPECTED FINDING: because this run re-processes an ALREADY-full 5030-chunk index end to end (not growing from empty like run-1), its per-batch holds are uniformly 4.7-11.6s, not just 'the last few batches' as in run-1 — see summary.residual_limitation.

runs.label: run-3: small incremental index (6 files touched) — the realistic production shape (mcp/server.ts:162 starts up with incremental:true), used to capture a clean JIT SUCCESS sample.
runs.note: Reported 'files: 1 indexed, 1337 skipped' — 5 of the 6 touched files were already correctly stored (run-2 had reached them, under its own per-batch lock, before being killed) and were caught by the isFileUnchanged stability skip (§7.1); only the genuinely-still-different file was rewritten. No data was lost or corrupted by killing run-2 mid-flight.

runs.label: jit-probe-A (FAILURE, full-reindex contention): checkAndRefreshIfStale during run-2's hold window
runs.command: node f1-jit-probe.mjs packages/core/injector/container.ts  (direct call, mirrors mcp/tools/_helpers.ts's jitRefreshFile)
runs.note: Landed inside one of run-2's uniformly-multi-second batch holds (see raw_events, two 'failed' jit-staleness events at waitMs:306, structurally identical shape to baseline's failure). This is the honest residual limitation — see summary.residual_limitation.

runs.label: jit-probe-B (SUCCESS, realistic incremental contention): checkAndRefreshIfStale during run-3's hold window
runs.note: This is the baseline's exact failure scenario (jit-staleness contending with an in-flight index run) now succeeding — waitMs:1 to acquire, holdMs:284 for the JIT's own single-file re-parse+write, well inside its 3x100ms retry budget.

raw_events: ... (run-1: 340 acquired/released 'index-run' events total, 170 batches; see summary for percentiles) ...
... (run-2 starts: uniformly long holds against the already-full index) ...
... (run-2 killed here, several more long holds) ...

structure_hold_ms.note: Headline: max single hold drops from 280,782ms to 11,078ms — a 25x reduction. Median hold (28ms) matches MAST_SPEC.md:824's 10-50ms per-file-parse claim closely, but the tail does not: as the FTS/graph index grows within a run, per-batch populateFile cost climbs superlinearly (GITNEXUS_COMPARISON.md §15.2, ~70% of pipeline time, out of scope for F1 — Stage 2/SQLite migration is the documented fix for the cost itself). F1's contribution is bounding the BLAST RADIUS of any one hold to a single 16-file batch instead of the whole 1,335-file run, not eliminating per-batch cost growth.

structure_acquisitions_per_run.note: 170, not the ~84 the task anticipated from LANCE_BATCH alone (1337/16=84 batches) — pass 1 (chunk-store+graph write) and pass 2 (edge insertion) are BOTH batched at LANCE_BATCH size and BOTH need their own lock (insertEdges/insertReExportFiles also mutate the graph db), giving ~84+84=168, plus 1 deleted-file-cleanup acquisition and 1 final manifest/index.json acquisition = 170. Documented in the runIndex WHY-comment (src/indexer/index.ts) and in the PR report — flagging the discrepancy from the task's estimate rather than silently reporting a number that doesn't match its own raw events.

jit_staleness_full_reindex_contention.outcome: failed (2 samples, both waitMs:306, structurally identical to the baseline failure)
jit_staleness_full_reindex_contention.note: residual_limitation (see below) — a full (non-incremental) reindex of an ALREADY-populated corpus has uniformly multi-second batch holds, which can still exceed the JIT path's 3x100ms retry budget for any single probe. This is a real, honest limitation of F1 alone; it directly matches IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md Stage 1's own note: 'F1 is still required — that's mitigation, not a fix' (Stage 2 shrinks it further).

jit_staleness_incremental_contention.note: This is the realistic production shape: mcp/server.ts:162 starts `mast serve` with incremental:true, so an in-flight background reindex is normally small (a handful of changed files, few/short batches). Here JIT succeeds cleanly, matching the automated test in src/indexer/__tests__/lock-scope.test.ts.

summary.residual_limitation: F1 converts the worst case from 'JIT starved for the ENTIRE run duration' (up to 280s, unconditionally) to 'JIT starved for at most one batch's write phase' — but does not by itself guarantee that a batch's write phase always fits the JIT retry budget. For a full/non-incremental reindex of a corpus whose index is already large (chunks.lance / FTS5 tables already near full size for the whole run, not growing from empty), per-batch populateFile cost is high enough (~5-11s, GITNEXUS_COMPARISON.md §15.2) that a JIT probe landing inside that specific batch can still fail. This is the documented, in-scope-for-Stage-2 (not F1) part of the problem; IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md already anticipates it ('Stage 2 shrinks the stale window as a side effect... F1 is still required — that's mitigation, not a fix').
